newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins steady,eye US data,ignore Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins steady,eye US data,ignore Eurobond.

text.p: MinFin bonds were little changed in nervous trading on Friday ahead of U.S. statistics and dealers said the market would be steady until the next meeting of the Fed to discuss U.S. interest rates on March 25.

"Trading was rather nervous ahead of the U.S. figures (announced at 1330 GMT), with prices weakening slowly. The PPI index was positive for the market and prices recovered some 0.30," an ICFI Moscow Partners Bank dealer said.
U.S. Treasury prices rose on news of a 0.4 percent drop in the PPI in February, the biggest drop since October 1994.
Dealers said the market shrugged off news Russia would issue two more Eurobonds in 1997 for at least $2 billion.
Finance Minister Alexander Livshits said one of the issues will be dollar-denominated, while in 1998 Russia could also issue rouble Eurobonds.
"Russian Eurobonds are in some way of less importance for the market than the news about U.S. interest rates, which is predominant now," a Moscow Narodny Bank dealer said.
Dealers forecast range-trading was likely to dominate the market until March 25 when the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meets to deliberate interest rates.
